title: Layer-adaptive INT8 calibration service and runtime kernel hook integration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Many production models show per-layer activation magnitude skew that causes naive per-tensor INT8 quantization to degrade generation quality. We need a service-driven pipeline that builds per-layer scale/shift profiles (activation-aware) and ships those profiles to the serving runtime as kernel hooks that adapt quantization parameters at inference time. This ticket covers the calibration service, the profile format, CI for accuracy regression testing, and runtime kernel integration with safe fallback behavior.
goal: Deliver a layer-adaptive INT8 calibration service that produces validated compensation profiles and a minimal runtime kernel hook API that applies profiles with graceful fallbacks, reducing mean generation quality regression to <1% on benchmark prompts while improving token throughput by >=1.8x vs FP16 for target models.
technical_approach: 1) Calibration agent: run activation collection across representative sample batches, compute per-layer scale and shift (and optional per-channel stats), support layer grouping and remapping for fused kernels. 2) Profile format: compact JSON/flatbuffer with model fingerprint, sequence-length buckets, and confidence metrics. 3) Validator: automated A/B prompt set eval harness to compare to FP16 outputs using n-gram and semantic metrics. 4) Runtime hooks: lightweight kernel adapters that accept profile, include safety thresholds, and expose metrics for sampling. 5) CI gating: accuracy/regression checks and perf microbenchmarks in runtime-1.22 pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: - Service emits profiles for at least 5 reference models (Llama2-13B, Mistral-small variant etc) documented in README. - Validator shows <1% delta on primary eval set (perplexity and semantic similarity) for canary models. - Runtime applies profile without increased p99 latency beyond 5% over current INT8 baseline. - Fallback to FP16 or default INT8 must be automatic on missing profiles or out-of-bound activations. - End-to-end e2e test added to CI with mock profiles.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for profile ingestion and validation. - Synthetic activation replay suite covering extreme activation skew. - A/B evaluation on curated prompt set (500 prompts) measured with BLEU/ROUGE and embedding cosine similarity. - Perf matrix across sequence lengths [32,128,512] and batch sizes to measure throughput and latency. - Nightly quant-regression job for top-customer models, alert on >1.5% quality drop.
implementation_notes: - Prefer flatbuffer profile layout to reduce serialization overhead; fallback JSON allowed for debug. - Use sequence-length bucketing to select kernel path. - Kernel hooks run in C++ runtime; expose a small C API and a rust wrapper used by the serving process. - Maintain telemetry counters for 'applied_profile', 'fallback_reason', 'profile_mismatch'.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Profiles overfit to calibration data causing unseen regressions. Mitigation: require cross-sample validation and per-profile confidence metrics; enable conservative scaling by default. Risk: CPU cost of profile select logic. Mitigation: precompute critical-path decisions and cache per-device. Risk: kernel ABI churn. Mitigation: versioned profile schema and compatibility checks.
rollout_plan: - Alpha: internal models only (runtime-1.22-alpha) with profile opt-in flag. - Beta: selected customer models and Dedicated pilot; collect telemetry and run nightly regressions. - GA: enable by default with ability to opt-out per-deployment. - Provide migration doc and CLI tool to generate profiles.
notes: Design review 2025-02-25: agreed to prefer per-layer shift in addition to scale to address heavy ReLU-skewed activations.
Experiment 2025-03-02: initial profiles reduced int8 quality gap by 0.8% on L2-13B validation set. PR#4123 adds kernel hook prototype.
